subject: Silo pinning: confirmation checklist & forensic-ready tombstone handoff
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@blueoak.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueOak Security <security@blueoak.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Silo pin confirmation and evidence needed for compliance review

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the earlier demo. Our compliance team needs a short checklist and evidence package showing that BlueOak’s dedicated tenant will be pinned to a single country region (no cross-region replicas), and that when we request deletion you will perform a coordinated tombstone + snapshot destruction with verifiable artifacts.

Specifically we need to confirm: 
- That the dedicated pool for our tenant will be region-anchored (region name: us-west-2) and not burst to other regions.
- How snapshots/backups are handled (are there automatic cross-region backups?).
- The retention window for logs and the exact procedure/timeline for a tenant-initiated erase (what artifacts we get back: deletion manifest, list of snapshot IDs scrubbed, log hashes).

Could you send a checklist we can attach to our internal audit, plus example evidence (redacted) of a completed wipe for another customer or a sample manifest?

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Director, Procurement & Security
BlueOak Financial

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we support region-pinned Dedicated pools and provide a forensic-ready wipe manifest on request. Im copying Ben (ops) and Marissa (CS lead) to put together the checklist and a redacted sample manifest.

Proposed deliverables (we can adjust):
- Region pin confirmation (signed statement of architecture and routing policy)
- Backup & snapshot behavior doc (explicitly call out cross-region backup behavior)
- Erase procedure & timeline (what we do within 24/72/120 hrs depending on replication state)
- Redacted sample: deletion manifest + snapshot ID list + SHA256 log hashes (suitably redacted)

Ben/Marissa: can you prepare the artifacts for BlueOak and propose an ETA? Also flag anything we cant redact because of other customer sensitivity.

Irene Choi
Head of Security Integrations, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0148

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Silo pin confirmation and evidence needed for compliance review

Irene / team — ops can produce everything requested. High level items and constraints below: 

1) Region anchoring
- We can pin the tenant to us-west-2 at provisioning. Smart routing will honor the pin; fallback policies will not move serving to another region unless explicitly enabled by the customer. That means requests, model serving, and KV/prefix caches are region-bound.

2) Snapshots & backups
- Our managed snapshot flow for Dedicated stores ephemeral runtime snapshots in the region by default. We have optional cross-region archival, but that is an opt-in feature — we do not enable cross-region backups unless the customer signs the archival opt-in.
- Exported snapshot files for BlueOak (if requested during erase) will list internal snapshot IDs; we will provide a scrubbed CSV of snapshot IDs we destroyed. Example filename: snapshot-ids-blueoak-20260303.csv

3) Erase procedure & timeline
- Step 0: Delete request received and validated (T0).
- Step 1 (T0+24h): Stop serving, revoke active KV cache, mark tenant tombstone in control-plane ledger.
- Step 2 (T0+24-72h): Trigger snapshot destruction job in-region; remove ephemeral caches.
- Step 3 (T0+72-120h): Expunge logs and run verification sweeps; produce deletion manifest (redwood-wipe-manifest-<date>.json) and a small forensic log (forensic-log-sample-<date>.txt) containing SHA256 hashes of relevant snapshots and key events.

4) Evidence format
- We can provide: deletion manifest (JSON), snapshot-id CSV, and SHA256 digests of scrubbed files. All artifacts are cryptographically signed by Redwood's KMS key id: rw-kms-2024-07.

5) Constraints
- We cannot share raw customer snapshot contents.
- Redacted manifests will replace customer identifiers with stable tokens.

ETA: I can assemble a redacted sample set and the checklist by EOD Tue (2026-03-03). I will attach the three artifact stubs and a short checklist.

Ben Carter
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Thanks Ben/Irene — that covers most of our questions. Two quick clarifications before we finalize the audit packet: 

1) If a customer has enabled long-term archival (the opt-in), can you enumerate where that archive could reside (regions or external S3 accounts)? We need to ensure our legal team can sign off.
2) For the deletion manifest: will Redwood include the KMS key ID used for signing? We need the signature chain in the manifest for our auditors.

If you can include those two items in the sample set, we should be able to close this. Also please confirm a sample SLA statement that committing to region pinning won´t be silently violated under load — we need language we can add to the contract redlines.

Regards,
Maria

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, contracts@blueoak.com

Maria — attaching the redacted sample artifacts and a short checklist; below are the clarifications you asked for.

Attachments included (redacted stubs):
- redwood-wipe-manifest-20260303.json (deletion manifest, includes manifest version, scrubbed snapshot list, timestamp, and signature metadata - KMS id: rw-kms-2024-07)
- snapshot-ids-blueoak-20260303.csv (list of internal snapshot IDs that were destroyed; IDs are stable tokens; CSV header explains redaction mapping)
- forensic-log-sample-20260303.txt (SHA256 hashes of deleted artifacts + verification timestamps)

Clarifications: 
- Archival opt-in: if a customer opts into archival, archives are stored in the customer-approved region(s). We support archival to the same region (us-west-2) or to a named secondary (e.g., us-east-1) only if the customer signs the archival addendum. We will not copy archives to third-party S3 outside those regions unless explicitly configured and contracted.
- KMS signing: the deletion manifest contains a signature object with the KMS key id we used (rw-kms-2024-07) and a signing timestamp. We provide the public verification key and a small verification script on request.
- Contract language: sample clause we can include — "Redwood Inference will not relocate tenant serving or snapshots outside the contracted region (us-west-2) without prior written consent. Emergency cross-region fallback is an opt-in, auditable feature and will be treated as a contractual exception." Ben, can you provide a one-paragraph SLA insertion and single-line escalation path?

If this looks good I can route the artifacts to your legal and compliance SIDs and we can sign the addendum.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Security Integrations, Redwood Inference
